profile_enrichments.short_biography: Researcher whose personal site and research page list Hany Farid coauthored deepfake and media-integrity publications from 2022-2026.
profile_enrichments.evidence_text: Farid's site provides the explicit URL. Maty Bohacek's research page lists multiple publications with Hany Farid, including 2022-2026 deepfake/media-integrity work.

profile_enrichments.short_biography: PhD 2026 alum from Farid's alumni list; personal publication page lists Hany Farid coauthorships in 2025 and 2026.
profile_enrichments.evidence_text: Farid's site provides the explicit URL and lists Justin Norman as Ph.D. 2026. Justin Norman's publication page lists Hany Farid coauthorships in 2025 and 2026.

profile_enrichments.short_biography: Research scientist at Adobe; completed a UC Berkeley PhD in 2021 advised by Hany Farid and works on digital forensics/media authenticity.
profile_enrichments.evidence_text: Personal site says she is a research scientist at Adobe, did her PhD at UC Berkeley advised by Hany Farid, and lists Farid coauthored forensics work. Berkeley dissertation page lists Shruti Agarwal's 2021 dissertation with Hany Farid as advisor.

profile_enrichments.short_biography: SUNY Distinguished Professor at University at Buffalo; Dartmouth PhD alum whose dissertation lists Hany Farid as first advisor.
profile_enrichments.evidence_text: Dartmouth dissertation page lists Siwei Lyu, 2005 Ph.D., first advisor Hany Farid. University at Buffalo profile identifies Siwei Lyu as SUNY Distinguished Professor. His publication page lists Hany Farid coauthorships from 2002-2005.

profile_enrichments.short_biography: Senior lecturer at Lancaster University researching digital technology, deception, forensic identification, and AI; listed by Farid as a 2020 postdoc.
profile_enrichments.evidence_text: Lancaster profile identifies Sophie Nightingale as a senior lecturer with digital-technology, deception, forensic-identification, and AI research interests. Berkeley/Farid pages and Farid's own site list Nightingale/Farid coauthored work and the Hany site lists her as postdoc 2020.

profile_enrichments.short_biography: Dartmouth PhD 2013 alum; personal publications page lists his dissertation advisor as H. Farid and multiple Kee/Farid publications.
profile_enrichments.evidence_text: Eric Kee's publication page lists Photo Forensics from Partial Constraints as his 2013 Dartmouth Ph.D. dissertation with advisor H. Farid, plus multiple Kee/Farid publications. DBLP and Dartmouth sources independently tie Eric Kee to Dartmouth/Farid work.

profile_enrichments.short_biography: University of Queensland profile identifies Priyanka Singh as having conducted postdoctoral research at Dartmouth and collaborated closely with Hany Farid.
profile_enrichments.evidence_text: University of Queensland profile says Priyanka Singh conducted postdoctoral research at Dartmouth College and collaborated closely with Hany Farid. OpenReview lists postdoc at Dartmouth from 2017-2019 and Hany Farid as postdoc advisor.

profile_enrichments.short_biography: Computer vision executive with a Dartmouth CS PhD; Dartmouth technical-report evidence ties Senthil Periaswamy to Hany Farid coauthored work.
profile_enrichments.evidence_text: LinkedIn snippet lists Dartmouth College education from 1996-2003 in image processing/computer vision. The Org profile says Senthil Periaswamy has a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Dartmouth and current/executive computer vision roles. Dartmouth Digital Commons lists Senthil Periaswamy and Hany Farid coauthoring technical reports.

profile_enrichments.short_biography: Computer vision and image forensics researcher whose Dartmouth PhD work with Hany Farid developed lighting and optical tools for detecting image tampering.
profile_enrichments.evidence_text: Dartmouth dissertation record identifies Micah Kimo Johnson's PhD thesis with first advisor Hany Farid. Personal MIT page says his PhD work developed digital forensic techniques and lists Hany Farid as a current collaborator. Hany Farid's alumni list has Kimo Johnson as Ph.D. 2007. LinkedIn result is plausible but not needed as the primary anchor.
